clue.text: Take heed of pupil's request to English teacher?

definitions.meaning: an instruction to pay close attention to what the speaker is saying
a schoolchild asking the teacher to grade an essay, read literally

explanation.surface: A warning to listen, or a pupil handing in homework and asking for it to be graded.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock idiom ordering a listener to take serious note of a prediction or warning.

clue.text: Officer on board that's keen, apparently

definitions.meaning: Colonel ... is a suspect in the board game Cluedo
the saying 'keen as ...' means very eager

explanation.surface: A naval officer on a ship who seems enthusiastic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; it is the Cluedo board, where Colonel Mustard is a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: The condiment is linked to keenness in the idiom 'keen as mustard' and names a Cluedo colonel.

clue.text: Courses reported? They go underground

indicators.note: said aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: routes are courses taken

explanation.surface: Someone asking about courses that are said to run below ground, like tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant roots grow down into the soil, beneath the surface.

clue.text: Miss chap welcoming trendy baker from Drury Lane

indicators.note: taking in a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to muff a catch is to miss it
a man is a chap
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A young woman greets a fashionable baker from a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a woman but is the verb. The nursery rhyme asks 'Do you know the muffin man, who lives on Drury Lane?'
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the muffin seller is said to live on Drury Lane, a London street.

clue.text: Hit with something meaty

parts.note: ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: Striking someone with a piece of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wham is a heavy forceful blow, so a hit.

clue.text: Question type ignoring a student's eloquence

indicators.note: leaving out, so letters are dropped from the question type

parts.note: a rhetorical question is one asked for effect
L, for learner, stands for a student, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A kind of question that ignores a student's eloquent speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain, so L is a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive or eloquent speaking and writing.

clue.text: Operator rejects working in rush

indicators.note: turns away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients
on means working, functioning

explanation.surface: A machine operator refuses to work in a rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operator' suggests a machine or phone operator; it is one who operates on patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a sudden powerful forward rush, as of water or a crowd.

clue.text: The old having turned up, head outside to find pop singer

indicators.note: the head word goes around the other piece

parts.note: bonce is British slang for head

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read backwards

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: An old person turns up and goes outside to meet a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head; YE reversed is EY.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyoncé is an American pop and R&B singer.

clue.text: Mr Fawlty and I regularly chat in church

parts.note: Basil Fawlty is the hotelier in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word chat

explanation.surface: Basil Fawlty and the speaker chatting regularly in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Fawlty, played by John Cleese, runs the hotel in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church, often granted special privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: One oversensitive bit of skin on end of chin — it hurts shaving

indicators.note: a bit of the word skin is just its opening letter
the end of the word chin is its closing letter

parts.note: ow is what you cry when something hurts
a shaving is a thin sliver, a flake

explanation.surface: A man nicks a flake of skin off the tip of his chin while shaving and winces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaving' looks like part of the barbering scene but supplies FLAKE; 'on' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern slang for a person thought too easily offended or emotionally fragile is a snowflake.

clue.text: Waiting game?

definitions.meaning: willing, up for something, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: A question about some pastime that involves waiting around.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses describe someone prepared: set to go, and willing to have a go.

clue.text: Attack in trouble after a case of shingles

indicators.note: the trouble piece comes after the shingles pieces in the answer
the case of a word is its outer shell, the first and last letters

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell, in trouble

explanation.surface: Someone suffering an attack of illness after a bout of shingles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of shingles' reads as a medical case but means the outside letters, S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is a verb meaning to attack violently, whether physically or with words.

clue.text: Rhapsody might follow this unconventional type

definitions.meaning: Queen's song title puts Rhapsody straight after this word
an artistic free spirit living outside social norms

explanation.surface: A musing about a free-spirited person whom a rhapsody might follow.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen's hit song 'Bohemian Rhapsody' supplies the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian is a person, often artistic, who lives an unconventional, free-spirited life.

clue.text: Top politician served superbly, backing Leave

indicators.note: going backwards, so the assembled letters are read in reverse

parts.note: PM is short for Prime Minister
a tennis player aces an opponent with an unreturnable serve

explanation.surface: A prime minister playing tennis superbly while backing the Leave campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' looks like the Brexit campaign but is the plain verb; 'backing' reverses PMACED.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly or secretly, a synonym for leave.

clue.text: Tory with nerve for challenge

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
front means cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician with the nerve to mount a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront is to face up to and challenge someone directly.

clue.text: Small, like a beer

definitions.meaning: the size of a typical British serving of beer

explanation.surface: Something tiny compared to a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a person or thing that is little, often humorously, as if measurable by the glass.

clue.text: Kid at home disrupted work on stage

indicators.note: thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child at home disturbing a parent's work in the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, a work performed on stage.

clue.text: Relative allowed to hold up golf glove

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting pieces sit below the golf letter, holding it up

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an aunt is a relative
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An aunt is permitted to hold up a golf glove.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a stout glove with a long flared cuff.

clue.text: Lion and swan fighting for one result of match?

indicators.note: the letters of the two creatures scrap and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion and a swan battling it out as an event result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a sporting contest but is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is a marriage, and marrying gives you relatives by law, including the husband of a daughter.

clue.text: Explode with terrible threats

indicators.note: the letters are in a terrible state, mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone explodes in rage, issuing terrible threats.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter is to break suddenly into pieces, as in an explosion.

clue.text: Socialist keeps fighting for payment

indicators.note: holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: red is the traditional colour and nickname of a socialist
war is fighting between nations

explanation.surface: A left-winger keeps on struggling for proper pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is a sum paid in recognition of a service, such as information leading to an arrest.

clue.text: Lady seen in oddly dour game

indicators.note: taking the odd-numbered letters of the word dour

parts.note: chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A noblewoman spotted playing a rather gloomy game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a noblewoman of high rank, entitled to be addressed as a lady.

clue.text: Some object, nag or rant about being conceited

indicators.note: turned about, so the hidden run is read backwards
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run hiding inside

explanation.surface: Someone who objects, nags or rants is complained about for being full of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'object, nag or rant' backwards gives TNARROGANTCEJBO, holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrogant and conceited are synonyms for having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance.

clue.text: Relish got us cooking

indicators.note: cooking the books means falsifying, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone got us making a relish in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relish' suggests a chutney in the kitchen scene, but means enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means hearty enjoyment or zest, as does relish.

clue.text: Superhuman born Greek

parts.note: b is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
Ionic is a Greek dialect and order of architecture

explanation.surface: A superhero who was born in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bionic means having electronically enhanced body parts, giving powers beyond the normal human.

clue.text: News to cover broadcast in Scottish town

indicators.note: the outer letters wrap over the inner piece

parts.note: N stands for new, so plural news gives two of them
to air is to broadcast

explanation.surface: Television news covering a broadcast from a town in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairn is a seaside town in the Scottish Highlands on the Moray Firth.

clue.text: Blunder and almost blow up?

indicators.note: nearly all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: to go off is to explode

explanation.surface: A mistake that very nearly caused an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is an informal word for a silly mistake.

clue.text: About to leave Jersey's capital

indicators.note: the abbreviation for about must depart from the jersey word

parts.note: a jersey is a tunic, with the apostrophe s added
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to leave the capital of Jersey, Saint Helier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey's capital' suggests St Helier; it is a garment and the definition 'capital' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunis is the capital city of Tunisia in North Africa.

clue.text: Observe a Liberal meeting former president's twin

parts.note: to look is to observe
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Watching a Liberal politician meet a former US president's identical twin.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookalike is a person who closely resembles another, like a twin or double.

clue.text: Off-limits, like a tired jumper?

definitions.meaning: someone who jumps but is now worn out, having no leaps left

explanation.surface: A forbidden area, or an exhausted athlete who has run out of jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means beyond permitted boundaries, so forbidden territory, and punningly bereft of leaps.
